subject: Halo Retail — Loadproof playbook & acceptance checklist
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena@haloretail.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Initial onboarding — workload profile and targets

Hi Kimberly —

Thanks for the intro call yesterday. Attached is the sample production workload snapshot we discussed (small/med/peak rows) and a short note on our expected traffic pattern over the next 90 days. We want to make sure the Redwood deployment meets our latency and throughput requirements before we promote to production. High-level expectations:

- Typical steady throughput: ~320 req/s (text-generation, seq_len=256)
- Peak bursts: up to 650 req/s for 3–8 minute windows
- Latency goal: p95 < 140ms, p99 < 380ms when not in peak bursts
- Tail tolerance: 99.9% < 500ms for SLA acceptance

Can you confirm what test harness you prefer (wrk-based loadgen or your internal harness) and whether you need additional sample prompts or auth tokens? Also note procurement (procurement@haloretail.com) will want to see a short acceptance checklist and a final results PDF for their records.

Attached: halo_sample_workload.csv (usage profile)

Thanks,
Elena
Director, Platform Engineering
Halo Retail

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Feb 2028 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Halo Retail — Loadproof playbook & acceptance checklist

Elena — great detail, thanks for the snapshot. High-level reply and proposed plan below.

TL;DR — We can run our Redwood loadproof harness against the sample workload you provided. Proposed acceptance targets (based on your ask + conservatism for canary):
- Functional acceptance: All responses are valid for a representative prompt set (we'll use the 200 prompts you provided)
- Performance acceptance: p95 latency < 120ms, p99 latency < 350ms, 99.9% < 450ms under steady-state; allow short burst exceptions during 3–8 minute peaks
- Throughput acceptance: sustain 500 req/s steady for 10 minutes with burst handling to 700 req/s for <= 8 minutes without SLA violation
- Error budget: <= 0.1% 5xx errors during the test window

Proposed schedule (this week):
1) Tuesday — onboarding load plan sign-off (we'll finalize concurrency, token limits, and prompt set)
2) Wednesday — dry run (low-concurrency smoke)
3) Thursday — full loadproof run (one steady 30-minute window + a burst window)
4) Friday — results review + acceptance decision

Action items for you: share the final prompt set and confirm whether we should test on your dedicated pool or Redwood-hosted staging. If you prefer, we can run the tests in your Dedicated environment (requires onboarding the test key) — let us know.

Attachments: none in this message.

Thanks — looping Monica and Ben to own execution.

— Kimberly Park
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Halo Retail — Loadproof playbook & acceptance checklist

Kimberly / Ben —

I'm adding the concrete load plan and the commands we'll run. I uploaded load_plan_v1.yaml to the shared drive (link above). Summary of the plan here:
- Load harness: redwood-loadgen v2 (continuous batching enabled, prefix/KV caching disabled for baseline)
- Worker nodes: 4x A100 equivalent GPUs (staging pool)
- Concurrency profile: ramp 50 -> 500 over 8 minutes; hold 500 for 30 minutes; inject a 7-minute burst to 700 then cool down
- Metrics captured: per-request latency (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999), GPU utl, mem usage, queue depth, token cost
- Artifacts: raw prometheus export, aggregated CSV, and a summarized PDF (attached after run)

Questions for Halo:
1) Do you have any prompts that must always return within 80ms for UX reasons? If so, mark them in the prompt set.
2) Confirm whether we should enable token-level logging for the run (adds ~5% overhead)

Attachments: load_plan_v1.yaml (plan stub)

-Monica

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Izzy Lang <izzy.lang@haloretail.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Feb 2028 13:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Halo Retail — Loadproof playbook & acceptance checklist

Izzy / Team —

We completed the dry run this morning (smoke) and then executed the full loadproof window at 10:30 AM PST. Highlights from the preliminary run (artifacts attached):
- Steady 30-minute window at 500 req/s: p95 = 112ms, p99 = 320ms, 99.9% = 420ms
- Burst window to 700 req/s for 7 minutes: p95 = 130ms, p99 = 390ms, 99.9% = 530ms (note: a small number of tail spikes during the burst)
- Error rate: 0.03% 5xx across the whole run
- GPU observations: slight queue buildup during burst; peak mem at 93% on worker-2

Attachments: halo_prelim_results.pdf, gpu_profile.log

I'm attaching the full CSV exports to the shared drive; will produce the summarized PDF by EOD. For acceptance, we passed steady-state requirements but the burst tail exceeded the initially stated strict 99.9% < 500ms by a small margin. Proposed mitigations: enable a short-lived autoscale policy for burst windows, or add an admission control layer to shed low-priority requests during bursts.

Ben
Benchmarking Engineer
Redwood Inference

Elena / Izzy —

Thanks and congratulations — this is a good outcome. Summary and final decision:

- Steady-state performance: PASSED (meets p95/p99 targets)
- Burst behavior: PARTIAL — tail exceeded 99.9% target during the 7-minute peak by ~30ms on a tiny fraction of requests
- Error goals: PASSED (well within budget)

Acceptance decision: GREENLIGHT to proceed to a controlled production canary with these conditions:
1) Enable short-lived autoscale for predicted marketing windows (we'll configure a 2x burst window for scheduled events)
2) Apply an admission control rule to shed low-priority background requests during burst windows
3) Ben to deliver final summarized acceptance PDF + CSV to Halo and procurement by EOD Friday
4) Vivek and Priyom will own the canary rollout and monitoring playbook (see link to internal runbook above)

Elena / Izzy, please confirm you accept the conditions above. Once Helena confirms, we will schedule a 1-hour go/no-go with your Platform team and move to canary.
